question: Does percepta spec-preflight (R9 pin 0.4.0) reproduce Indy-init's documented results on R8 and the three control packages?
hypothesis: H1-H5 of protocols/SPR-B4-01.md: exit 3 with INV-04, CommandEnvelope and DEV-R8-12 findings on v4.1.1; exit 0, nothing blocking on v4.1.2/v4.1.5/v4.1.6; no T18<->T20 finding; under 1 s.
independentVars: percepta version (4a53688 = v0.4.0 = HEAD; 0ad2bd3 first commit)
condition (DOC: 4 inputs incl. --catalog; CI: no --catalog, as preflight-tooling.yml)
comparison: B3 C1-loop/C2/C3/C4 on the same packages (B3 committed results, re-run from a scratch copy: identical)
startRevision: track 3b7c9f7 (preregistration); percepta 4a53688 and 0ad2bd3; Indy-init 1cb27ec, bc3c381, 89f5840, dae2347

environment.dotnet: SDK 10.0.402 at /root/.dotnet; self-contained linux-x64 publish (bundles .NET 8 runtime)

procedure: Identify the R9 pin from Indy-init toolchain.lock.json (bc3c381) and dependency-lock.json (dae2347): percepta-semantic-v0.4.0 = 4a53688.
git archive each percepta revision into /home/user/sprint-scratch/B4/src-<rev>; dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64 --self-contained (as package.sh), one build at a time.
Extract inputs with git show into /home/user/sprint-scratch/B4/inputs/<package>; record SHA-256.
Run each (version, package, condition) n times; record exit, report, stdout/stderr, perf_counter wall time.
Classify with preregistered matchers; build results.csv and comparison.json.
verification: harness/tests: 12 unittest tests (classify unit tests; results.csv and comparison.json regenerate exactly from raw; input hashes equal git blobs; all runs reproduced identical reports; preregistered expectations).
limitations: Local rebuild from the tagged source, not the downloaded release archive.
Controls are successive amendments of one specification and v4.1.2 was co-written with the tool; not independent.
Timing on a loaded host; includes process start-up.
conclusion: Docs claim reproduced exactly (VERIFIED). Both versions give byte-identical reports. Without --catalog the carrier defect is not detectable.
reproduction: cd tracks/B4-preflight; export PATH=/root/.dotnet:$PATH; (build as protocol) ; python3 -I harness/run_preflight.py --exe /home/user/sprint-scratch/B4/bin-4a53688/Percepta.Cli --version-label v0.4.0-4a53688 --out raw --runs 5; python3 -I harness/summarize.py; python3 -m unittest discover -s harness/tests -v

question: POST HOC: how general are spec-preflight's and B3's rules under defect-preserving rewrites of the R8 inputs?
hypothesis: Both rule sets depend on surface wording; rewrites that keep the defect will defeat some rules.
independentVars: probe P0-P7 (identity, reworded bound, per-minute bound, 2-cycle, effect synonym, irrelevant string field on the carrier, reworded catalog sentence, carrier renamed)
dependentVars: per-defect catch for spec-preflight and for B3 C1-loop, C1-cycle, C2, C3
comparison: spec-preflight v0.4.0 vs B3 checks (scratch copy) on identical mutated inputs

environment.dotnet: SDK 10.0.402 at /root/.dotnet; self-contained linux-x64 publish (bundles .NET 8 runtime)

procedure: Apply each rewrite to the extracted R8 inputs (and to B3's .fs stubs for type edits).
limitations: Post hoc; probes chosen by B4 after reading both rule sets (adversarial, not a random sample).
Only the R8 package is mutated; false-alarm generality is not probed.
conclusion: spec-preflight misses P1, P3, P4 (INV-04) and P5, P6 (carrier); survives P2 and P7. B3 C1-loop misses P3, P4 and on P1 alarms only via the wrong clause; C1-cycle survives P3; B3 C2 survives P5-P7 because it keys on type/field names containing 'Command'. Neither is generic.
